title: Which geometric category?
as_he_states: The finite-type objects over a noetherian quasi/pro-schematic object are a catégorie géométrique (?) with the displayed descent and quotient axioms.
plausible_today: Identify the exact category first; a topos or an exact extensive category is a possible reconstruction, not a transcription.
state_of_art: SGA4 IV1.1.2 and Theorem1.2 characterize a topos under explicit axioms including a small generating family and all disjoint universal sums. These extra hypotheses have not been shown for this category.
why_open: The pages give a question and conflicting category word, not an account of why the question was abandoned.
worth: Worth a bounded source-recovery run: it would determine what theorem is actually being proposed.

title: Finite colimits from the proposed axioms
as_he_states: After base change and sums: donc aux ... finies ???; the precise finite diagrams are uncertain.
plausible_today: In a topos pullback preserves colimits; for a weaker category one must separately establish the needed universal quotient and image properties.
state_of_art: SGA4 IV1.1.2 states universal sums and effective universal equivalence-relation quotients. No exact weaker-axiom implication was found.
why_open: The author marks the implication; no historical explanation of its later omission is supplied.
worth: Worth checking once MP61 fixes the category, because the claim can then be tested by a finite categorical argument.

title: Possible marginal question on inverse-limit subgroups
as_he_states: The glyph is 2|? beside the subgroup and density discussion; its status as a question is not secure.
plausible_today: For K in a projective limit, K is dense in the limit of its coordinate images; equality requires an additional completeness/closedness condition.
state_of_art: Bourbaki Topologie générale III section7 gives the limit subgroup framework; the cylinder proof is rechecked here. The finite-support subgroup of the product of F2 shows why equality is stronger.
why_open: No confirmed open question can be extracted from an undecided glyph.
worth: Worth only a scan check; the written density mathematics is settled.

title: Locality of the constructible-intersection notion
as_he_states: Nature locale de la notion ??, with uncertain name for the local intersection notion.
plausible_today: Patch closedness is local on a patch-open cover; on compact patch basis opens it is equivalent to compactness of each intersection. Abstract local compactness of a subset is not enough.
state_of_art: Stacks08YF Lemmas5.23.2 and5.23.5 support the spectral formulation. The local proof is recorded in narrative section3.
why_open: A questioned locality step survives; no source says why it was dropped.
worth: Worth a short source-and-hypothesis concordance, because this local notion feeds the later constructible categories.

title: Two disputed hypothesis flags
as_he_states: Pro reads too restrictive on108 and les vérifier on110; Codex reads always verified and sont vérifiées.
plausible_today: Every scheme morphism pulls back retrocompact opens and constructible subsets; qc maps need not send constructibles to constructibles.
state_of_art: Stacks054H Lemma29.23.1 proves pullback; Lemma29.23.2 and Theorem29.23.3 impose finite-presentation/type conditions for images. The generic singleton gives the direct negative test.
why_open: These may not be authorial doubts at all. The independent text reverses both readings.
worth: Worth high-priority ink checking; do not open a new research problem on the basis of the Pro wording.

title: Néron-spaces programme heading
as_he_states: Pro reads Pb à poser. Espaces de Néron!; Codex allows pts épais. Espaces de Néron. No detailed question is stated in this heading.
plausible_today: Use126–132 to recover the thick-point programme; do not infer a separate theorem from the title alone.
state_of_art: Greenberg1966 Theorem1 and BG18.2 give approximation and point realization, but neither supplies the omitted definition of a Néron space in this programme.
why_open: No specific unresolved proposition or reason for dropping it appears in the title.
worth: Worth retaining as programme provenance; mathematical work should start from MP67–71.

title: Equivalence of the thickness conditions
as_he_states: The four (Ép) conditions and arrows are written with questions; one arrow is labelled M.L. et I=N.
plausible_today: Under the precise source definitions, (Ép)′ implies genericity (Ép). Under noetherian stage hypotheses, constructibility of closure{x} is equivalent to eventual pullback of closure{x_i}. The complete four-way equivalence is not established.
state_of_art: Stacks0A2Y proves constructible descent in spectral inverse limits. Stacks0597 proves nonempty limits of countable nonempty ML set systems. Neither by itself identifies the missing scheme-level ML hypothesis.
why_open: The visible question marks and missing hypotheses explain the present identification obstruction; no later historical reason for abandonment was found.
worth: Worth a focused run: formulate the exact fibre/image ML condition and test the missing arrow against noetherian affine examples.

title: The undefined right-hand thickness implication
as_he_states: The arrow near ??? introduces X′_i and an inverse-image equality not defined on this leaf.
plausible_today: No strongest mathematical statement can responsibly be selected before X′_i and the arrow are read; possible closure and image interpretations must remain alternatives.
state_of_art: The spectral descent and ML results above are comparators only. Greenberg/Sebag searches did not recover this notation.
why_open: The question is explicit but its operands are not secure.
worth: Worth recovering from the scans before proof work; otherwise different statements would be conflated.

title: Local finite equations for a thick closure
as_he_states: The local prime-ideal fragment q⊃p iff q⊃f1...fn is abbreviated and interrupted.
plausible_today: On D(g), require sqrt(pA_g)=sqrt((f1,...,fn)A_g); the f_i are a list of equations, not necessarily a product.
state_of_art: Constructible closed subsets of an affine spectral space have quasi-compact open complement and hence finitely generated radical defining ideals; this is the finite Boolean mechanism in Stacks04ZC and0A2Y.
why_open: The fragment has no completed arrow or explicit research question; retain as an unfinished proof step.
worth: Worth a short reconstruction after MP68, because it can make the thickness criterion algebraically testable.

title: Greenberg thick points and finite-index maps
as_he_states: Proposition1 asserts existence, thick image, k(y)⊂k(x), and a finite-index promorphism near the closure for a dominant generically separable rational map.
plausible_today: The valuative set map exists where the generic map is defined and the target is proper. Preservation of the unidentified thick notion, field descent and finite-index morphicity require separate hypotheses.
state_of_art: BGv6 Proposition18.2 supplies complete-DVR point realization. Stacks0BX5 gives unique proper extension. Sebag preprint7.2.1–2 gives a bounded-Jacobian cylinder comparison with smoothness and dimension hypotheses. No exact finite-index claim was located.
why_open: No proof or definition of finite index is present here; sources do not say why the author left the assertion unproved.
worth: Worth substantial source recovery before a mathematical run: the present field-perfectness distinction is essential.

title: Bounded simple pieces and constructible Greenberg images
as_he_states: Proposition2 uses X_K-simple subsets and a bounded ell|d invariant to obtain constructible image and a finite morphic partition.
plausible_today: A bounded-Jacobian/defect cylinder image theorem is true in the explicit smooth-source framework of Sebag; identification with the page’s simple/ell/index conditions remains unproved.
state_of_art: Greenberg1966 Theorem1 gives linear approximation; Sebag preprint4.3.12 gives constructible finite-level cylinder images and7.2.2 gives a cylinder-image result with bounded data. They do not settle the unexpanded manuscript quantifiers.
why_open: The sheet is an assertion, not a securely marked conjecture; missing definitions prevent an exact fate assignment.
worth: Worth a high-interest run after definition recovery, not a broad claim that motivic integration settled it.

title: Laurent ind-scheme notation and strict stages
as_he_states: The explicit caution is abus de langage ici!; the nonisomorphism sentence has n′≥n, which fails at equality.
plausible_today: The coefficient functor is an ind-affine group; for strict n′>n its fixed-valuation stage inclusions are not isomorphisms.
state_of_art: Osipov–Zhu Lemma2.1 gives Laurent-unit factorization. This run proves the precise bounded-stage assertions by coordinate equations and dual-number witnesses.
why_open: The caution concerns notation. The equality boundary is a transcription/statement issue, not evidence of a surviving open theorem.
worth: Worth an ink check and a clean source commentary; no further proof-development task is required for the checked assertions.

title: Pro-scheme Hom with only quasi-compact sources
as_he_states: The comparison is asserted with finite presentation for target stages and a quasi-compact insertion for source stages.
plausible_today: The comparison is established for qcqs source stages and affine transition maps; the broader qc-only source wording is not certified here.
state_of_art: Stacks01ZC Proposition32.6.1 explicitly uses quasi-separatedness to descend gluing equalities; EGAIV8.13.1 is the historical comparator.
why_open: The page provides no explanation whether quasi-separatedness was implicit or overlooked.
worth: Worth a short convention audit before seeking counterexamples to the broader reading.

title: Which group of nilpotent coordinate changes?
as_he_states: The sheets switch between evaluation on a nilpotent ideal, an augmented jet algebra, coefficient parameters and an undefined tangent module.
plausible_today: Augmentation-preserving truncated-algebra automorphisms require zero constant term and unit linear determinant. Nilpotent translations give bijections on m^n but need not preserve the naive polynomial truncation ideal.
state_of_art: Stacks00UP gives formal étale lifting; Stacks04FJ gives the lift torsor. The two earlier-run counterexamples and full quadratic composition are rerun here.
why_open: The calculation is unfinished and its ambient object is not fixed; no source records a reason for abandonment.
worth: Worth a precise functor-of-points formulation, limited to the source’s finite nilpotent level before generalization.

title: Withdrawn formulations

plausible_today: These are source-history entries, not live open mathematical problems. Surviving replacements are tracked separately in claims402,417,422,430.
state_of_art: SGA4 IV and Olivier give comparisons for the surviving material, but they do not reveal the author’s reason for these particular cancellations.
why_open: Only same-sheet withdrawal is evidenced; archive order does not date the revisions.
worth: Worth retaining for the companion commentary; do not assign new research work to cancelled claims.

title: Scope of the isolated Lie-cohomology exercise
as_he_states: An exercise concludes H^p(g,M)=0 using an invertible operator T=dρ+ρd, but its representation-theoretic antecedents lie elsewhere.
plausible_today: If T is an invertible chain map homotopic to zero, the complex is contractible via T^−1ρ. This does not imply unrestricted Lie-cohomology vanishing.
state_of_art: Bourbaki LieI exercise context is a publication comparator; the exact omitted antecedents were not recovered from an accessible full edition. The chain-homotopy lemma is directly proved.
why_open: Missing reused pages, not evidence of a new open conjecture.
worth: Worth only a source-concordance task if this exercise is used in the archive commentary.
